About 1 in 10. Fewer than 1 in 100 need chest compressions or drugs.

What are the five signs of the Apgar score?
Appearance (colour), pulse, grimace (reflex irritability), activity (tone) and respiration.
When is the Apgar score done?
At 1 and 5 minutes, then every 5 minutes during resuscitation.
Is resuscitation delayed until the 1-minute Apgar score?
No. The decision is made on breathing, heart rate and tone.
Within the first minute the baby is dried, kept warm, the airway is cleared if needed and the baby is stimulated; if the baby is not breathing, ventilation starts by 60 seconds.
What are the indications for bag-and-mask ventilation?
Apnoea, gasping, or a heart rate below 100/min.
How many inflation breaths are given first?
Five inflation breaths, followed by ventilation breaths.

What oxygen concentration is used to start the resuscitation of a term baby?
Room air (21%); 21–30% for babies born before 35 weeks.
What is the best sign of effective ventilation?
A rising heart rate, with chest movement.
When the heart rate stays below 60/min after 30 seconds of effective ventilation.
What is the compression-to-ventilation ratio in the newborn?
3 : 1, which is 90 compressions and 30 breaths per minute.
How are neonatal chest compressions done?
With two thumbs on the lower third of the sternum, compressing to one third of the depth of the chest.
A meconium-stained baby is not vigorous. What is the first action?
Ventilation is started within the first minute. Routine tracheal suction is not done.
What is the indication for adrenaline?
A heart rate below 60/min despite 30 seconds of good ventilation and chest compressions.
What is the intravenous dose of adrenaline in the newborn?
10–30 µg/kg, which is 0.1–0.3 ml/kg of adrenaline 1:10 000, through the umbilical vein.

When does the team consider stopping resuscitation?
When there is no heart rate after about 20 minutes of full resuscitation.
How is a baby with a diaphragmatic hernia resuscitated?
The baby is intubated at once; bag-and-mask ventilation is avoided, and a nasogastric tube is passed.
During bagging, a baby suddenly deteriorates and one side of the chest is silent. What is the cause and the treatment?
A pneumothorax, treated by needle decompression.
